subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is the continuous roof-like overhead layer formed by the leafy branches and foliage of tall trees in a dense forest called?
explanation: The canopy is the uppermost continuous ceiling formed by the interlocking leafy crowns of mature tall trees in a forest.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is the branchy upper part of an individual tree above the stem or trunk called?
explanation: The crown is the top portion of a tree comprising branches, twigs, and foliage radiating outward above the trunk.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What are the horizontal vegetation layers of smaller trees, shrubs, tall herbs, and grasses growing beneath the high canopy called?
explanation: The understorey consists of intermediate vegetation strata (small trees, shrubs, bushes, herbs) thriving in the shade below the canopy.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: Why are forests celebrated and referred to as the 'GREEN LUNGS' of our planet?
options: Through photosynthesis, forest trees release vast amounts of OXYGEN into the atmosphere and absorb CARBON DIOXIDE, maintaining atmospheric gas balance
Because trees are green in color
Because leaves look like human lungs
explanation: Forests regulate planetary gas exchange: green plants fix carbon dioxide and release life-sustaining oxygen during photosynthesis.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What are the specialized micro-organisms (bacteria and fungi) that break down dead plant and animal matter into dark, nutrient-rich HUMUS called?
explanation: Decomposers recycle organic biomass by converting decaying detritus into dark fertile humus that replenishes soil nutrients.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: How do forest tree root systems and the forest floor prevent destructive FLASH FLOODS and SOIL EROSION?
options: The thick forest floor and root networks act as a giant natural sponge, slowing down rainwater runoff, allowing water to seep into the ground to recharge groundwater
Trees block rain from falling from clouds
Trees push water into the ocean directly
Trees turn rainwater into solid ice
explanation: Forest leaf litter and dense root networks decelerate raindrops, arrest surface runoff, facilitate groundwater percolation, and bind topsoil.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is 'SEWAGE' in environmental science?
options: Liquid wastewater produced by households, industries, hospitals, and commercial establishments carrying dissolved and suspended contaminants
Clean drinking water from mountain streams
explanation: Sewage is municipal liquid waste carrying fecal matter, detergents, pathogens, organic refuse, and hazardous chemical contaminants.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What does the technological abbreviation 'WWTP' stand for in municipal water management?
explanation: A Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) is a facility that removes physical, biological, and chemical pollutants from sewage water.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: In the first primary stage of a WWTP, what mechanical filters are used to screen out large physical debris such as rags, plastic bottles, sticks, and cans?
explanation: Bar screens are vertical metal grids that intercept and remove coarse floating solids (plastics, rags, wood) from raw sewage.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is the semi-solid organic matter that settles at the bottom of the large central sedimentation tank (clarifier) in a WWTP called?
explanation: Sludge is the settled organic particulate matter scraped from clarifier bottoms, subsequently digested in anaerobic bio-reactors.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What common disinfectant chemical (or gas) is added to treated wastewater before releasing it into rivers to kill harmful disease-causing microbes?
explanation: Chlorination (or UV irradiation/ozonation) oxidizes and eradicates pathogenic bacteria, viruses, and parasites before environmental discharge.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: Which fast-growing tree species is recommended to be planted alongside wastewater sewage ponds because it absorbs surplus wastewater rapidly and releases pure water vapor into the air?
explanation: Eucalyptus trees have high transpiration rates, absorbing large volumes of wastewater and purifying groundwater bio-ecologically.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: Why is a forest referred to as a 'DYNAMIC LIVING ENTITY — FULL OF LIFE AND VITALITY'?
options: It sustains an interconnected web of diverse flora, fauna, insects, and decomposers where nutrients are endlessly recycled, energy flows continuously, and life regenerates autonomously
Because trees walk around at night
Because it is powered by electric generators
Because humans plant every tree every year
explanation: Forest ecosystems exhibit complex trophic self-regulation: producers, consumers, and decomposers recycle matter in an enduring dynamic equilibrium.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What occurs during the 'AERATION' stage in a modern Wastewater Treatment Plant?
options: Compressed air is vigorously pumped into clarified wastewater to stimulate the rapid growth of AEROBIC BACTERIA that consume human waste, food residue, and soaps
Water is frozen into solid ice blocks
Water is boiled in giant furnaces
Chemicals are added to dye the water blue
explanation: Aeration tanks supply dissolved oxygen to heterotrophic aerobic microorganisms, accelerating the biological decomposition of organic pollutants.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: How is the organic 'Sludge' collected from clarifier tanks beneficially utilized in sustainable waste management?
options: It is transferred to closed digester tanks where ANAEROBIC BACTERIA decompose it, producing BIOGAS (used as fuel/electricity) and nutrient-rich manure for farming
It is thrown into the ocean
It is turned into plastic toys
It is burned as coal in train engines
explanation: Anaerobic sludge digestion yields methane-rich biogas for renewable energy and sterile bio-solids for agricultural soil fertilization.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: Why should used cooking oils and animal fats NEVER be poured down domestic kitchen sink drains?
options: Fats harden and solidify inside drain pipes, clogging plumbing, and in open drains they block soil pores, impairing natural water filtration
Fats attract fish into the pipes
Fats make water smell like roses
explanation: Cooking fats congeal into stubborn 'fatbergs', obstructing sewer lines and coating soil particles, which impedes wastewater filtration.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: Why should discarded chemical paints, solvents, motor oil, and expired medicines not be thrown into toilets or drains?
options: These toxic chemicals kill the beneficial microbes in wastewater treatment plants that naturally break down sewage waste
They cause water to turn into solid rock
They make water too clear to see
explanation: Toxic chemicals and pharmaceuticals poison the beneficial biocatalytic bacterial populations essential for biological sewage purification.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is a 'Septic Tank' on-site sewage disposal system?
options: A watertight underground settling chamber where sewage decomposes anaerobically; suitable for isolated homes, rural hospitals, or clusters of houses without municipal sewer networks
A large tank that stores clean rainwater
A truck that transports bottled water
explanation: Septic tanks provide decentralized on-site anaerobic sewage digestion and effluent soil absorption for unsewered locations.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is the 'Vermi-Processing Toilet' developed and tested successfully in India?
options: A low-cost, hygienic, water-saving toilet system where earthworms (like red worms) completely process human excreta into high-nutrient vermicompost cakes
A toilet connected to car engines
A toilet that uses chemical gases
explanation: Vermi-toilets utilize earthworms to bioconvert human fecal sludge into odorless, pathogen-free, high-grade organic vermicompost.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: How do forests influence the local atmospheric CLIMATE and the WATER CYCLE?
options: Forests transpire enormous volumes of water vapor into the air through their leaves, cooling the ambient climate, increasing atmospheric humidity, and inducing rainfall
Forests heat the air like stoves
explanation: Evapotranspiration from forest canopies generates regional atmospheric moisture flux, lowering surface temperatures and promoting convective precipitation.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: Consider a typical forest food chain: Grass → Insects → Frog → Snake → Eagle. What happens if all the FROGS are removed from this ecosystem?
options: The population of insects will explode and damage vegetation, while snakes will face food scarcity and starve, destabilizing the food web
Nothing will change in the forest
explanation: Trophic cascade: removing intermediate secondary consumers (frogs) triggers pest outbreaks at lower levels and predator starvation at higher levels.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is 'Scum' in a WWTP sedimentation clarifier tank?
options: Light, floatable impurities such as oils, grease, and fats that float on the water surface and are removed by a specialized mechanical skimmer
explanation: Low-density floatable contaminants (fats, oils, grease) float to the surface as scum and are skimmed off mechanically.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is 'Grit and Sand Removal' in a WWTP?
options: Wastewater passes through a tank at a reduced velocity so that heavy coarse sand, grit, and small pebbles settle down by gravity
Water is filtered through silk cloth
Water is spun in a centrifuge
Sand is added to make water cleaner
explanation: Velocity retardation in grit chambers causes dense mineral particles (sand, gravel) to precipitate out without settling organic matter.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: Why does deforestation lead to severe SOIL EROSION and LAND DEGRADATION?
options: Tree roots physically bind the soil together; in the absence of trees, heavy rain and wind wash away the fertile topsoil, turning fertile land into barren desert (desertification)
Because dead roots turn into water
Because wind cannot blow in forests
explanation: Arbor root networks anchor soil horizons; deforested slopes suffer catastrophic topsoil sheet wash, rill erosion, and desertification.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What deadly water-borne diseases are transmitted by untreated municipal sewage contaminating drinking water sources?
options: Cholera, Typhoid, Dysentery, Hepatitis, and Polio
explanation: Untreated fecal wastewater contains microbial pathogens (Vibrio cholerae, Salmonella typhi, Entamoeba) that cause lethal diarrheal epidemics.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is 'Activated Sludge' produced in the aeration tank of a WWTP?
options: A concentrated biological mass consisting of millions of active aerobic bacteria, protozoa, and suspended organic matter (~97% water)
explanation: Activated sludge is a living microbial floc of active aerobic decomposers that digest organic pollutants in aeration basins.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is the primary role of forest tree canopy in regulating the impact of HEAVY MONSOON RAINS on soil?
options: The multi-tiered canopy intercept the falling raindrops, breaking their kinetic velocity so that water drips gently down branches and trunks, preventing soil compaction
It completely evaporates all rain before it reaches the ground
It reflects rain back into clouds
explanation: Canopy interception dissipates the destructive kinetic energy of torrential rain, converting erosive downpours into gentle stemflow and leaf drip.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is a 'Manhole' in urban municipal sewerage systems?
options: An access opening located every 50 to 60 metres along sewer lines, at junctions and bends, allowing sanitary workers to inspect, clean, and unblock underground pipes
A place to store drinking water
A doorway into a subway train
A trash bin on the street
explanation: Manholes provide vital physical maintenance entry points along subterranean sewer networks at standardized intervals and directional junctions.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): Forests act as natural self-sustaining water purification and flood control systems.
Reason (R): The dense root systems bind soil particles, while the porous organic humus on the forest floor facilitates deep vertical rainwater infiltration, preventing runoff surges and continuously recharging subterranean aquifers.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Forest hydrology: the spongy leaf litter and root bio-matrix maximize infiltration capacity, preventing surface floods and sustaining baseflows.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following sequence of Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) unit operations:
Group:
1. Bar Screening - Intercepts large floating rags and plastic items
2. Grit Chamber - Settles coarse mineral sand and pebbles by gravity
3. Aeration Basin - Aerobic bacteria digest soluble organic wastes
4. Sugar Crystallizer - Adds chocolate syrup to sweeten drinking water
options: Unit 4 (WWTP processes involve physical clarification, biological digestion, and chemical disinfection; they NEVER add confectionery sugars or chocolate syrup)
explanation: Unit 4 is an absurd distortion: municipal wastewater engineering uses disinfection (chlorine/UV/ozone), not confectionery sweeteners.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question:
Analyze the biological mechanism of 'Biochemical Oxygen Demand' (BOD) in wastewater analysis:
Why is a high BOD in sewage effluent dangerous for aquatic life?
options: High BOD indicates a massive load of organic pollutants; as aerobic bacteria consume dissolved oxygen to decompose this waste, oxygen levels in the river plummet to near zero, causing catastrophic fish suffocations
High BOD turns water into acid that melts fish scales
High BOD freezes the river solid
High BOD increases river water salinity to ocean levels
explanation: BOD quantifies the oxygen consumed by microbes decomposing organic waste. High BOD causes severe aquatic anoxia, killing fish and invertebrates.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question:
Match Column I (WWTP Treatment Stages) with Column II (Primary Environmental Functions):
(a) Bar Screens         -> (i) Mechanical removal of coarse solid plastic/rag debris
(b) Aeration Basin      -> (ii) Aerobic microbiological oxidation of dissolved organic wastes
(c) Anaerobic Digester  -> (iii) Methanogenic fermentation of sludge producing combustible biogas
(d) UV / Chlorination   -> (iv) Pathogen disinfection and destruction of waterborne bacteria
explanation: Bar screens = coarse screening; Aeration = aerobic oxidation; Digester = biogas generation; Chlorination = pathogen disinfection.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question:
Read the statements regarding forest ecology:
Statement 1: In a climax virgin forest, no waste is generated because every decaying organic matter is decomposed and recycled into nutrients.
Statement 2: Diverse canopy strata provide distinct ecological niches, supporting high biodiversity of birds, mammals, and insects.
Statement 3: Forests produce toxic carbon monoxide that destroys the ozone layer.
Which statements are TRUE?
explanation: Statement 3 is an absurd falsehood (forests produce oxygen). Statements 1 (zero-waste biogeochemical cycling) and 2 (canopy microhabitats) are true.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is the biological role of 'Fungi and Micro-arthropods' in the humification process on the forest floor?
options: They secrete extracellular enzymes that digest recalcitrant plant polymers (lignin, cellulose), transforming leaf litter into stable, dark, mineral-rich colloidal humus
They eat living tree trunks and kill the forest
They convert soil into solid glass
They absorb all sunlight on the ground
explanation: Saprophytic fungi (white-rot, brown-rot) and soil micro-arthropods enzymatically cleave complex lignin/cellulose polymers into nutrient-rich humus.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: How do constructed wetland bio-filtration systems (like Phytoremediation reed beds) purify sewage water without electricity?
options: Aquatic plants (like reeds and cattails) absorb heavy metals and excess nitrogen/phosphorus, while microbial biofilms around their root zones biologically degrade organic pollutants
By boiling water using solar mirrors
By adding chemical dyes that hide dirt
By freezing sewage into ice bricks
explanation: Phytoremediation leverages rhizosphere microbiology and macrophyte bio-accumulation to remediate wastewater naturally and passively.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question:
Consider four environmental management practices:
1. Reclaiming methane biogas from anaerobic sewage digesters for clean electricity
2. Planting multi-species agroforestry green belts around industrial zones
3. Discharging untreated raw factory effluents into freshwater rivers
4. Using vermicompost from human waste toilets as organic soil conditioner
Which of these practices represent SUSTAINABLE CIRCULAR BIO-ECONOMY?
explanation: Practice 3 is environmentally destructive pollution. Practices 1, 2, and 4 embody closed-loop circular resource recovery.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: Why does the presence of high levels of Coliform Bacteria (such as E. coli) in a river or well indicate severe water pollution?
options: Coliform bacteria are natural inhabitants of the human and warm-blooded animal intestinal tract; their presence proves direct contamination by raw sewage and high risk of lethal enteric pathogens
Because they produce poisonous radioactive gases
Because they make water turn red
explanation: Coliforms serve as universal microbiological fecal indicator organisms, demonstrating sewage contamination and the presence of enteric waterborne pathogens.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What is the physical cause of 'Eutrophication' in freshwater lakes receiving untreated domestic sewage and detergent runoff?
options: Excessive nitrogen and phosphate nutrients trigger explosive algal blooms; when the algae die, decomposing bacteria consume all dissolved oxygen, suffocating aquatic animals
The lake gets too cold to support fish
Detergents turn water into solid jelly
Algae turn into large carnivorous plants
explanation: Nutrient hyper-enrichment (phosphates/nitrates) drives algal blooms whose subsequent decomposition induces severe lake hypolimnetic anoxia.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: How do deep-rooted forest trees prevent Hillside LANDSLIDES during torrential cloudbursts?
options: The extensive taproot and lateral root networks act as bio-mechanical anchors, interlocking soil strata and bedrock, while continuous transpiration drains excess soil pore-water pressure
Trees build stone walls with their branches
explanation: Arbor roots provide tensile soil reinforcement, increasing mechanical shear strength and relieving pore-water pressure that triggers slope failure.

subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Forests: Our Lifeline & Wastewater Story
question: What supreme ecological synthesis concludes the NCERT Class 7 Science curriculum in Chapter 12?
options: Human health, ecological balance, clean water, and planetary survival depend inextricably on conserving living forest biomes as our vital life-support systems and adopting responsible, closed-loop circular sanitation to keep our water bodies pure and vibrant
That nature can be destroyed without consequences
That technology will replace all natural forests
explanation: Chapter 12 synthesizes forest conservation, hydrological cycles, ecological stewardship, and circular environmental engineering.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: A geometric line that divides a plane figure into two identical, matching halves such that one half completely folds over and covers the other is called a:
explanation: A line of symmetry is an axis of reflection that bisects a figure into two congruent, mirror-image halves.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: How many lines of symmetry does an EQUILATERAL TRIANGLE have?
explanation: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry passing through each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: How many lines of symmetry does a regular SQUARE have?
options: 4 Lines of Symmetry (2 through midpoints of opposite sides, 2 along diagonals)
explanation: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: 2 vertical/horizontal medians and 2 diagonal lines.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: How many lines of symmetry does a CIRCLE have?
options: Infinitely Many Lines (any diameter is a line of symmetry)
explanation: A circle has an infinite number of lines of symmetry passing through its center along any diameter.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is the smallest angle through which a figure is rotated around a central point to look EXACTLY THE SAME as its original position called?
explanation: The angle of rotation is the minimum angle of turn around the center of rotation that maps the figure onto itself.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is the ORDER OF ROTATIONAL SYMMETRY of a square in one complete 360° turn?
explanation: A square maps onto itself 4 times during a 360° rotation (every 90°), hence its rotational symmetry order is 4.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is the ORDER OF ROTATIONAL SYMMETRY and ANGLE OF ROTATION of a RECTANGLE (non-square)?
explanation: A rectangle looks identical twice in a complete turn (at 180° and 360°), so order = 2 and angle of rotation = 180°.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: How many FACES (F), VERTICES (V), and EDGES (E) does a standard 3D CUBE have?
explanation: A cube has 6 square faces, 8 corner vertices, and 12 straight edges.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is EULER'S FORMULA relating Faces (F), Vertices (V), and Edges (E) for any convex polyhedron?
options: F + V - E = 2 (or F + V = E + 2)
explanation: Euler's Polyhedral Formula: F + V - E = 2 holds universally for all simple convex polyhedra.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: A flat 2D skeletal pattern or layout that can be folded along its edges to construct a 3D solid shape is called a:
explanation: A net is a 2D planar unfolded diagram consisting of adjacent polygons that fold together to construct a 3D polyhedron.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is the cross-section obtained when a vertical cut (slicing) is made through an apple or a circular cylinder?
explanation: A horizontal cut through a cylinder gives a circle; cutting an apple transversely also yields a circular cross-section.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: Which English capital letter has BOTH horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry as well as rotational symmetry of order 2?
explanation: Letter 'H' possesses 2 lines of symmetry (horizontal and vertical) and rotational symmetry of order 2 (180°).

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: How many lines of symmetry does a REGULAR HEXAGON have, and what is its order of rotational symmetry?
options: 6 Lines of Symmetry and Order of Rotational Symmetry = 6 (Angle of rotation = 60°)
explanation: A regular n-gon has n lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order n; for a regular hexagon, n = 6 (angle = 360°/6 = 60°).

explanation: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 6 vertices, and 9 edges, satisfying Euler's formula (5 + 6 - 9 = 2).

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: How many FACES, VERTICES, and EDGES does a SQUARE PYRAMID have?

explanation: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 base + 4 triangular sides), 5 vertices (4 base + 1 apex), and 8 edges.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is the difference between an OBLIQUE SKETCH and an ISOMETRIC SKETCH of a 3D solid?
options: An oblique sketch does not preserve exact proportional dimensions of receding depths ; an isometric sketch is drawn on an isometric dot grid where exact scaled measurements are preserved
Oblique sketches are drawn with circles only
Isometric sketches are drawn without rulers
explanation: Isometric projections use a 30° equilateral triangular dot grid preserving scale proportions along axes, unlike oblique pictorial sketches.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: On a standard playing DIE (Dice), the sum of the numbers of dots on opposite faces is ALWAYS equal to:
explanation: Standard dice convention: opposite faces always sum to 7 (1+6=7, 2+5=7, 3+4=7).

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is the cross-section shape obtained when you make a VERTICAL SLICE through a solid Brick (Cuboid)?
options: A Rectangle (or Square depending on cut)
explanation: A vertical or horizontal planar slice through a cuboid always yields a rectangular (or square) cross-section.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is the cross-section obtained when you make a VERTICAL SLICE through the apex of a solid CONE?
explanation: A vertical axial cross-section passing through the apex of a right circular cone produces an isosceles triangle.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: Which of the following geometric figures has ONLY Rotational Symmetry of Order > 1 but NO Line of Symmetry?
options: A Parallelogram (Rotational symmetry of order 2, but 0 lines of symmetry)
explanation: A standard non-rhombic parallelogram has rotational symmetry of order 2 (180°), but zero reflectional lines of symmetry.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a regular PENTAGON?
explanation: A regular pentagon has order 5 and angle of rotation = 360°/5 = 72°.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: Three cubes each of edge 2 cm are placed side-by-side to form a single CUBOID. What are the dimensions (length, breadth, height) of the resulting cuboid?
options: Length = 6 cm, Breadth = 2 cm, Height = 2 cm (Length = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 cm)
Length = 2 cm, Breadth = 2 cm, Height = 2 cm
Length = 6 cm, Breadth = 6 cm, Height = 6 cm
Length = 8 cm, Breadth = 2 cm, Height = 2 cm
explanation: Placing 3 identical cubes of side 2 cm linearly results in a cuboid of dimensions 6 cm × 2 cm × 2 cm.

subject: Mathematics

question: Can a polyhedron have 10 faces, 20 edges, and 15 vertices?

NO, because F + V - E = 10 + 15 - 20 = 5 ≠ 2 (violating Euler's formula)

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What solid shape is generated when a right-angled triangular sheet is rotated rapidly around one of its perpendicular sides as the axis?
explanation: Rotating a right-angled triangle around its altitude sweeps out a 3D right circular cone.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: What solid shape is generated when a flat rectangular sheet is rotated rapidly around one of its sides?
explanation: Rotating a rectangle around one edge generates a 3D circular cylinder.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question: How many lines of symmetry does a RHOMBUS have?
options: 2 Lines of Symmetry (along its two diagonals)
explanation: A non-square rhombus has exactly 2 lines of symmetry coinciding with its perpendicular diagonals.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): Every regular polygon of 'n' sides possesses both 'n' lines of reflectional symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 'n'.
Reason (R): Regular polygons have equal sides and equal interior angles, mapping onto themselves under reflections across vertex-bisectors/side-medians and rotations of (360°/n).
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Fundamental theorem of polygonal symmetry: an n-sided regular polygon exhibits dihedral symmetry group D_n with n reflection axes and n-fold rotation.

chapter: Chapter 12: Symmetry & Visualising Solid Shapes

Spot the IMPOSTER in the following polyhedra and their Euler characteristic components (F, V, E):

1. Cube - F=6, V=8, E=12 (6 + 8 - 12 = 2)

3. Square Pyramid - F=5, V=5, E=8 (5 + 5 - 8 = 2)

chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is 'Ocean Acidification' caused by rising atmospheric carbon dioxide levels?

Ocean water turning into fresh drinking water
explanation: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃; seawater acidification depletes carbonate ions, imperiling coral reefs (Great Barrier Reef) and marine food webs.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: Which global conservation organization publishes the authoritative 'IUCN RED LIST' of threatened biological species?
options: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
explanation: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of biological species.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is the 'Great Green Wall' initiative in Africa?
options: An ambitious 8,000-km ecological restoration project planting a continuous belt of trees across the entire width of the Sahel to halt the southward expansion of the Sahara Desert
A giant concrete wall built along borders
explanation: The Great Green Wall combats desertification across 11 Sahelian nations by restoring 100 million hectares of degraded land by 2030.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is 'Mission LiFE' (Lifestyle for Environment) launched by India at the 2021 Glasgow Climate Summit?
options: A global mass movement encouraging individuals and communities to adopt sustainable, mindful, environmentally conscious everyday consumption choices instead of mindless consumerism
A medical insurance plan for doctors
A space satellite mission to study life on Mars
explanation: Mission LiFE mobilizes citizens worldwide as 'Pro-Planet People' (P3) to reduce waste, save water, conserve energy, and practice circular lifestyles.

chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is 'E-Waste' (Electronic Waste) and why is its recycling critical?
options: Discarded electronic devices (smartphones, computers, batteries) containing hazardous heavy metals (lead, mercury, cadmium) as well as recoverable precious metals (gold, copper, lithium)
Old paper books thrown into garbage
explanation: E-waste recycling prevents neurotoxic heavy metals from leaching into groundwater while recovering critical rare earth elements and lithium.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is 'Microplastics' pollution?
options: Tiny microscopic plastic fragments (less than 5 mm in size) resulting from the degradation of plastic waste, synthetic textiles, and cosmetics that contaminate oceans, marine food chains, and human bloodstream
Small plastic coins used in board games
explanation: Microplastics (<5mm) ubiquitously pollute marine biospheres, bio-accumulating up trophic levels into fish, table salt, and human tissues.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What are 'Biodiversity Hotspots'?
options: Biogeographic regions that possess exceptionally high concentrations of endemic biological species (found nowhere else on Earth) and are undergoing severe habitat loss (e.g. Western Ghats and Eastern Himalayas)
explanation: Norman Myers defined 36 global Biodiversity Hotspots: regions with ≥1,500 endemic vascular plant species having lost ≥70% primary habitat.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is the 'Albedo Effect' in polar climate science?
options: The fraction of solar radiation reflected by a surface: white polar ice has high albedo (reflects ~80% sunlight), but melting ice exposes dark ocean water which absorbs heat, accelerating global warming in a feedback loop
The color of polar bears' fur
The sound made by glaciers breaking
The depth of polar ice sheets
explanation: The ice-albedo feedback is a critical climate tipping element: loss of reflective sea ice increases oceanic heat absorption.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is 'Circular Economy'?
options: An economic model aimed at eliminating waste through continuous cycles of designing for durability, reuse, repairing, refurbishing, and recycling materials indefinitely
An economy that prints round coins only
Trading goods only in circular markets
An economy where prices go in circles
explanation: The circular economy replaces the linear 'take-make-dispose' paradigm with closed-loop regenerative resource cycles.

options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question:

What happens when a population exceeds the carrying capacity of its environment?

The ecosystem instantly doubles in size
Animals evolve into different species within a day
Nothing happens because nature has infinite resources
explanation: Carrying capacity (K) defines maximum sustainable population; ecological overshoot leads to resource depletion and demographic collapse.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is the biogeochemical danger of 'Permafrost Thawing' in the Arctic tundra regions?
options: Thawing permafrost awakens ancient microbes that decompose trapped organic matter, releasing hundreds of billions of tons of potent METHANE (CH₄) and CO₂ into the atmosphere, triggering runaway warming
It causes all rivers to turn into saltwater
It stops the Earth's magnetic field
explanation: Permafrost holds ~1,500 gigatons of frozen carbon—twice the carbon currently in the atmosphere; thawing creates a catastrophic carbon-feedback loop.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is 'Payment for Ecosystem Services' (PES) in environmental economics?
options: Incentives and financial compensations paid to local farmers, forest dwellers, and landowners who manage their land sustainably to provide vital ecological services (clean water filtration, carbon sequestration, flood prevention)
Taxes paid to enter city parks
Prices charged for buying bottled water
explanation: PES programs (e.g. Costa Rica's PSA) internalize ecological externalities by rewarding indigenous and rural communities for preserving living ecosystems.

They were corporate advertising campaigns for wood companies

question: What is the 'Loss and Damage Fund' established at COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh) and operationalized at COP28 (Dubai)?

A fund to pay insurance for broken cars
A bank loan for oil companies

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: Why are 'Mangrove Ecosystems' (like the Sundarbans) hailed as super-heroes of coastal climate resilience?
options: They store up to 5 times more carbon per hectare than tropical rainforests (Blue Carbon), buffer coastal communities against ferocious cyclone surges and tsunamis, and serve as vital nursery grounds for marine biodiversity
Because they produce pure gold crystals in their roots
Because they can walk across oceans
Because they prevent rain from falling
explanation: Mangroves are premier Blue Carbon sinks and bio-shields against coastal erosion, storm surges, and tsunami devastation.

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What is 'Ecological Footprint' articulated by Mathis Wackernagel and William Rees?
options: A metric that compares human consumption of natural resources against the Earth's biocapacity to regenerate those resources and absorb our waste; currently, humanity consumes resources at the rate of 1.7 Earths
The weight of human feet on soil
The number of trees planted in a garden
The distance animals travel every year
explanation: Ecological footprint measures human demand on natural capital versus planetary biocapacity (calculated annually on Earth Overshoot Day).

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 12: Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Renewable Energy & Sustainable Development
question: What supreme planetary ethical manifesto concludes the General Knowledge curriculum in Chapter 12?

That human beings should exploit every natural resource until nothing is left
That technology eliminates the need for nature
That environmental problems will solve themselves automatically
explanation: Chapter 12 culminates in the universal ethic of ecological stewardship: harmonizing human civilization with planetary boundaries for intergenerational sustainability.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Human Environment, Settlements, Transport, Communication & Life in Deserts

Because clouds are too heavy to fly over mountains
Because there is no sun in Ladakh

subject: Social Science

A mirage that disappears when approached
A mountain of gold in the sand
A dry salt flat with no water

Scattered settlements are built on boats

Because ships do not require any fuel
Because water flows in all directions automatically
Because water transport is faster than airplanes

The Brahmaputra river from Sadiya to Dhubri

Because the government ordered them to wear robes

Living without any shelter in winter

options: Topography, water availability, agricultural land fertility, and climate constraints dictating spatial human organization
Government orders telling people where to sleep
The color of local soil only
Random chance with no geographic logic
explanation: Settlement patterns are structured by physical geography: water access, agrarian carrying capacity, defensive topography, and transport arteries.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Human Environment, Settlements, Transport, Communication & Life in Deserts
question: How did the ancient 'Silk Route' passing through the high Karakoram passes of Ladakh historically connect India with Central Asia, Tibet, and China?
options: Leh served as a bustling entrepôt caravan trade hub where Indian merchants traded spices, cotton, and dyes for Central Asian silk, raw wool, charas, and turquoise stones
Trade was carried out using submarine boats
It was a modern railway line built 2,000 years ago
It was an air route for flying carpets
explanation: Leh was a pivotal crossroad on the trans-Himalayan Silk Road network, linking Kashmir and Punjab to Yarkand, Kashgar, and Lhasa.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Human Environment, Settlements, Transport, Communication & Life in Deserts
question: Why is 'Information Highway' (High-Speed Fiber-Optic Broadband & 5G Satellite Internet) considered the modern equivalent of 19th-century railway networks?
options: Just as railways revolutionized the physical transport of freight and labor during the Industrial Revolution, high-speed digital networks transport massive data, finance, commerce, and knowledge instantly across the globe
Because fiber-optic cables are made of iron rails
Because internet cables carry physical train cars
Because internet was invented in the 19th century
explanation: Broadband data infrastructure is the 21st-century neural network of global capitalism, accelerating frictionless virtual commerce, research, and communication.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Human Environment, Settlements, Transport, Communication & Life in Deserts
question: What is the engineering challenge and significance of the 'Atal Tunnel' (Rohtang) and upcoming 'Zojila Tunnel' in the Himalayan transport network?
options: They provide all-weather, year-round strategic military and civilian road connectivity beneath avalanche-prone high passes, ending months of winter isolation for Ladakh and Lahaul-Spiti
They are built to store water
They are giant shopping malls inside mountains
They were constructed for tourist trains to Europe
explanation: Atal Tunnel (9.02 km) and Zojila Tunnel (14.2 km) conquer extreme mountain geography, ensuring year-round strategic and socioeconomic connectivity.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 12: Human Environment, Settlements, Transport, Communication & Life in Deserts
question: What grand humanistic and geographic perspective concludes the NCERT Class 7 Social Science curriculum in Chapter 12?
options: Humanity is an integral part of the living Earth—our settlements, global transport networks, and communication technologies reflect our creative adaptability, demanding that we live in harmonious balance with natural ecosystems, respecting cultural diversity and conserving planetary resources for future generations
That human beings should conquer and destroy all natural environments
That deserts are useless wastelands that have no culture or life
That all humans should live in identical cities
explanation: Chapter 12 concludes the Class 7 Social Science curriculum by synthesizing human ecological adaptability, technological connectivity, and sustainable biocultural conservation.

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: सार्थक शब्दों का वह व्यवस्थित एवं क्रमबद्ध समूह जो किसी विचार या भाव को पूर्ण रूप से स्पष्ट करता है, क्या कहलाता है?
explanation: वाक्य: सार्थक शब्दों का व्यवस्थित एवं व्याकरण सम्मत समूह जिससे वक्ता का पूर्ण अभिप्राय स्पष्ट हो।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: व्याकरण की दृष्टि से वाक्य के मुख्य रूप से दो अनिवार्य अंग कौन-से होते हैं?
explanation: वाक्य के दो अनिवार्य घटक (अंग) होते हैं: उद्देश्य (जिसके बारे में बात हो) और विधेय (उद्देश्य के बारे में जो कहा जाए)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: वाक्य में जिसके विषय में कुछ कहा जाता है, उसे व्याकरण में क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: उद्देश्य: वाक्य में जिसके विषय में कोई विधान या बात की जाए, वह उद्देश्य (Subject) कहलाता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: वाक्य में उद्देश्य (कर्ता) के विषय में जो कुछ कहा जाता है, उसे क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: विधेय: उद्देश्य के बारे में कही गई समस्त बात/क्रिया विधेय कहलाती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: रचना की दृष्टि से वाक्य के मुख्य रूप से कितने भेद होते हैं?
options: 3 भेद (1. सरल वाक्य, 2. संयुक्त वाक्य, 3. मिश्र वाक्य)
explanation: रचना के आधार पर वाक्य के 3 भेद हैं: सरल वाक्य, संयुक्त वाक्य, तथा मिश्र वाक्य।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: अर्थ की दृष्टि से हिंदी में वाक्य के कुल कितने भेद होते हैं?
options: 8 भेद (विधानवाचक, निषेधवाचक, आज्ञावाचक, प्रश्नवाचक, विस्मयादिवाचक, इच्छावाचक, संदेहवाचक, संकेतवाचक)
explanation: अर्थ के आधार पर वाक्य के 8 भेद होते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: वाक्य के पूर्ण होने पर अंत में प्रयुक्त होने वाले विराम चिह्न (।) को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: पूर्णविराम (।): साधारण वाक्य की समाप्ति पर लगने वाला विराम चिह्न।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: पढ़ते या बोलते समय बहुत थोड़े समय के लिए रुकने हेतु प्रयुक्त होने वाले चिह्न (,) को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: अल्पविराम (,): वाक्य में न्यूनतम ठहराव दर्शाने के लिए प्रयुक्त चिह्न।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: किसी के कहे गए कथन को ज्यों-का-त्यों उद्धृत करने के लिए किस चिह्न (" ") का प्रयोग किया जाता है?
options: उद्धरण चिह्न या अवतरण चिह्न (Quotation Marks)
explanation: उद्धरण चिह्न (" "): प्रत्यक्ष कथन को मूल रूप में व्यक्त करने हेतु प्रयुक्त।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'ईद का चाँद होना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ क्या है?
explanation: 'ईद का चाँद होना': दुर्लभ होना या अत्यधिक लंबे अंतराल के बाद दिखाई देना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'नौ दो ग्यारह होना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ क्या है?
explanation: 'नौ दो ग्यारह होना' का अर्थ है तुरंत भाग जाना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'अधजल गगरी छलकत जाए' लोकोक्ति का सही अर्थ क्या है?
options: कम ज्ञान या योग्यता वाला व्यक्ति बहुत अधिक दिखावा और डींगें हाँकता है
explanation: 'अधजल गगरी छलकत जाए': ओछा या अल्पज्ञ व्यक्ति अपनी योग्यता का अत्यधिक आडंबर करता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: जिस वाक्य में केवल एक ही उद्देश्य (कर्ता) और एक ही समापिका क्रिया (विधेय) होती है (जैसे: 'सूर्य पूर्व में उदय होता है'), उसे क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: सरल वाक्य: जिसमें एक ही मुख्य उद्देश्य और एक ही विधेय समापिका क्रिया होती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: जब दो या दो से अधिक स्वतंत्र सरल उपवाक्य समानाधिकरण योजकों (और, तथा, एवं, या, किन्तु, परन्तु, इसलिए) से जुड़े होते हैं (जैसे: 'रात हुई और तारे निकल आए'), तो उसे क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: संयुक्त वाक्य: जहाँ स्वतंत्र सरल वाक्य समानाधिकरण समुच्चयबोधकों द्वारा जुड़े होते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: जिस वाक्य में एक मुख्य (प्रधान) उपवाक्य होता है और एक या अधिक आश्रित (गौण) उपवाक्य व्यधिकरण योजकों (कि, जो, क्योंकि, यदि-तो, जब-तब, जैसा-वैसा) से जुड़े होते हैं, उसे क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: मिश्र वाक्य: जिसमें एक प्रधान उपवाक्य पर एक या अधिक आश्रित उपवाक्य निर्भर होते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'यदि तुम कठिन परिश्रम करोगे, तो अवश्य सफल होगे।' अर्थ की दृष्टि से यह किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
options: संकेतवाचक वाक्य (Conditional Sentence - एक कार्य का होना दूसरे पर निर्भर)
explanation: संकेतवाचक वाक्य: जहाँ एक क्रिया का होना दूसरी क्रिया पर शर्त या संकेत के रूप में निर्भर करता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'भगवान करे, तुम्हारी यात्रा मंगलमय हो।' अर्थ की दृष्टि से यह किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
options: इच्छावाचक वाक्य (शुभकामना / इच्छा प्रकट करने वाला)
explanation: इच्छावाचक वाक्य: जिससे वक्ता की इच्छा, आशीर्वाद या शुभकामना का बोध हो।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'शायद आज शाम को वर्षा होगी।' अर्थ की दृष्टि से यह किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
options: संदेहवाचक वाक्य (संभावना / संदेह प्रकट करने वाला)
explanation: संदेहवाचक वाक्य: जिसमें कार्य के होने में संदेह या संभावना का भाव हो।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: लिखते समय जब कोई शब्द या अंश छूट जाता है, तो उसे पंक्ति के ऊपर लिखकर किस त्रुटिपूरक चिह्न का प्रयोग किया जाता है?
explanation: हंसपद / काकपद (^): लिखते समय छूटे हुए शब्द को पंक्ति के ऊपर दर्शाने हेतु प्रयुक्त चिह्न।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: शब्दों को संक्षिप्त रूप में लिखने के लिए किस चिह्न (जैसे: पं०, डाॅ०, कृ०पृ०उ०) का प्रयोग किया जाता है?
explanation: लाघव चिह्न (०): बड़े शब्दों के संक्षिप्त रूप (Abbreviation) को प्रदर्शित करने के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'अंगूठा दिखाना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ क्या है?
options: ऐन वक्त पर साफ़ इनकार कर देना / मना कर देना
explanation: 'अंगूठा दिखाना': आवश्यकता के समय सहायता करने से स्पष्ट मना कर देना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'दाँत खट्टे करना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ क्या है?
options: शत्रु को बुरी तरह पराजित करना / हरा देना
explanation: 'दाँत खट्टे करना': युद्ध या मुकाबले में विरोधी को परास्त कर देना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा' लोकोक्ति का सही अर्थ क्या है?
options: अपनी अयोग्यता या कमी को छिपाने के लिए साधनों या दूसरों में दोष निकालना
explanation: 'नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा': स्वयं काम न आने पर परिस्थिति या उपकरण में दोष मढ़ना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा' लोकोक्ति का सही अर्थ क्या है?
options: बहुत बड़ी आवश्यकता के लिए अत्यंत कम या अपर्याप्त मात्रा में वस्तु मिलना
explanation: 'ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा': अत्यधिक खुराक या आवश्यकता की तुलना में बहुत नगण्य वस्तु मिलना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'दूर के ढोल सुहावने होना' लोकोक्ति का सही अर्थ क्या है?
options: दूर से चीजें अच्छी और आकर्षक लगती हैं, परन्तु पास जाने पर वास्तविकता कुछ और होती है
ढोल की आवाज बहुत मीठी होना
explanation: 'दूर के ढोल सुहावने': दूर से वस्तुएँ मनोहर प्रतीत होती हैं किंतु यथार्थ में कठिनाइयाँ छिपी होती हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'मुहावरे' (Idiom) और 'लोकोक्ति' (Proverb) में क्या मूलभूत व्याकरणिक अंतर होता है?
options: मुहावरा एक 'वाक्यांश' (Phrase) होता है जो वाक्य में मिलकर प्रयुक्त होता है और जिसका लिंग-वचन के अनुसार रूपांतरण होता है ; जबकि लोकोक्ति एक 'पूर्ण स्वतंत्र वाक्य' (Full sentence) होती है जिसका रूप अपरिवर्तित रहता है
मुहावरा केवल संस्कृत में होता है
लोकोक्ति केवल एक शब्द की होती है
दोनों में कोई अंतर नहीं होता
explanation: मुहावरा वाक्यांश (अपूर्ण वाक्य) है जो वाक्य का अंग बनता है; लोकोक्ति पूर्ण स्वतंत्र अनुभव-सिद्ध वाक्य होती है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: निम्नलिखित में से 'शुद्ध वर्तनी' वाला शब्द कौन-सा है?
explanation: उत् + ज्वल = उज्ज्वल (दोनों 'ज' अर्ध/आधे होते हैं)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: निम्नलिखित में से 'व्याकरणिक दृष्टि से शुद्ध वाक्य' का चयन कीजिए:
options: 'यहाँ शुद्ध गाय का दूध मिलता है।' -> अशुद्ध ; 'यहाँ गाय का शुद्ध दूध मिलता है।' -> शुद्ध
explanation: दूध शुद्ध होता है, गाय नहीं; अतः पदक्रम की दृष्टि से 'यहाँ गाय का शुद्ध दूध मिलता है' शुद्ध है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question:
कथन और कारण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें:
कथन (A): 'जब विपत्ति आती है, तब कोई साथ नहीं देता।' यह एक मिश्र वाक्य है।
कारण (R): इसमें 'तब कोई साथ नहीं देता' प्रधान उपवाक्य है तथा 'जब विपत्ति आती है' कालवाचक क्रियाविशेषण आश्रित उपवाक्य है, जो 'जब-तब' योजक से जुड़े हैं।
सही विकल्प चुनें:
options: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
explanation: मिश्र वाक्य संरचना: प्रधान उपवाक्य के साथ जब-तब से जुड़ा कालवाचक क्रियाविशेषण आश्रित उपवाक्य।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following classification of मुहावरे और उनके लाक्षणिक अर्थों में:
Group:
1. आँखें खुलना - वास्तविकता का ज्ञान होना / होश में आना
2. कान भरना - चुगली करना / भड़काना
3. फूले न समाना - अत्यधिक प्रसन्न होना
4. हाथ-पैर मारना - तैराकी प्रतियोगिता में पहला स्थान प्राप्त करना
options: युग्म 4 ('हाथ-पैर मारना' का लाक्षणिक अर्थ 'कठिन प्रयास / प्रयत्न करना' होता है, केवल तैराकी पदक जीतना नहीं)
explanation: युग्म 4 में 'हाथ-पैर मारना' का व्यापक मुहावरेदार अर्थ 'हर संभव प्रयास/उपाय करना' है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question:
सुमेलित कीजिए (विराम चिह्न और उनके मानक नाम):
(क) ;  -> (i) अर्धविराम (Semicolon)
(ख) :  -> (ii) उपविराम / अपूर्णविराम (Colon)
(ग) -  -> (iii) योजक चिह्न (Hyphen)
(घ) —  -> (iv) निर्देशक चिह्न (Dash)
explanation: ; = अर्धविराम; : = उपविराम; - = योजक; — = निर्देशक।

chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: मिश्र वाक्य में 'आश्रित उपवाक्य' (Subordinate Clauses) के तीन मुख्य प्रकार कौन-से होते हैं?
options: 1. संज्ञा आश्रित उपवाक्य (प्रायः 'कि' से जुड़े) ; 2. विशेषण आश्रित उपवाक्य (जो, जिसे, जिसका से जुड़े) ; 3. क्रियाविशेषण आश्रित उपवाक्य (जब-तब, जहाँ-तहाँ, जैसे-वैसे, क्योंकि, यद्यपि-तथापि से जुड़े)
explanation: आश्रित उपवाक्य के 3 भेद: संज्ञा उपवाक्य ('कि'), विशेषण उपवाक्य ('जो/जिसने'), क्रियाविशेषण उपवाक्य ('जब/जहाँ/जैसे/क्योंकि')।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'उसने कहा कि मैं निर्दोष हूँ।' इस वाक्य में रेखांकित उपवाक्य 'कि मैं निर्दोष हूँ' किस प्रकार का आश्रित उपवाक्य है?
options: संज्ञा आश्रित उपवाक्य (क्रिया 'कहा' के कर्म के रूप में प्रयुक्त)
explanation: 'कि' से प्रारंभ होकर मुख्य क्रिया के कर्म के रूप में आने वाला उपवाक्य संज्ञा आश्रित उपवाक्य कहलाता है।

question: 'जो लड़का कल आया था, वह मेरा मित्र है।' वाक्य में 'जो लड़का कल आया था' किस प्रकार का आश्रित उपवाक्य है?
options: विशेषण आश्रित उपवाक्य (संज्ञा 'लड़का' की विशेषता बता रहा है)
explanation: 'जो/जिसने' से प्रारंभ होकर प्रधान उपवाक्य की संज्ञा की विशेषता बताने वाला उपवाक्य विशेषण आश्रित उपवाक्य होता है।

chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: निम्नलिखित में से 'वाक्य रूपांतरण' (सरल से संयुक्त) का शुद्ध उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: सरल वाक्य: 'सूर्योदय होने पर कुहासा छँट गया।' -> संयुक्त वाक्य: 'सूर्योदय हुआ और कुहासा छँट गया।'
सरल वाक्य: 'सूर्योदय हुआ क्योंकि कुहासा छँट गया।'
सरल वाक्य: 'जब सूर्योदय हुआ तब कुहासा छँट गया।'
सरल वाक्य: 'सूर्योदय होते ही कुहासा छँटा।'
explanation: समानाधिकरण योजक 'और' जोड़कर दो स्वतंत्र उपवाक्यों में रूपांतरित करना शुद्ध संयुक्त वाक्य रचना है।

chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: निम्नलिखित वाक्यों में से 'अशुद्ध वाक्य' को पहचानिए:
options: 'कृपया करके मेरी बात सुनिए।' (अशुद्ध: 'कृपया' और 'करके' दोनों का एक साथ प्रयोग पुनरुक्ति दोष है ; शुद्ध: 'कृपया मेरी बात सुनिए' या 'कृपा करके मेरी बात सुनिए')
'साहित्य और समाज का घनिष्ठ संबंध है।'
'प्रत्येक बच्चे को दो-दो संतरे दिए गए।'
explanation: 'कृपया' और 'करके' का साथ प्रयोग वर्जित पुनरुक्ति दोष है; शुद्ध रूप: 'कृपया मेरी बात सुनिए'।

question: 'कवयित्री' और 'आशीर्वाद' शब्दों की शुद्ध वर्तनी वाला युग्म कौन-सा है?
options: कवयित्री और आशीर्वाद (क + व + यि + त्री ; आ + शी + र्वा + द)
explanation: शुद्ध वर्तनी: 'कवयित्री' (क-व-यि-त्री) तथा 'आशीर्वाद' ('व' के ऊपर रेफ 'र्')।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: 'गागर में सागर भरना' मुहावरे का सही और सटीक साहित्यिक अर्थ क्या है?
options: थोड़े से शब्दों में बहुत गंभीर, गूढ़ और विस्तृत अर्थ व्यक्त करना (जैसे बिहारी के दोहे)
मटके में समुद्र का पानी भरना
explanation: 'गागर में सागर भरना': अत्यंत संक्षिप्त एवं सारगर्भित पदावली में गहन अर्थ का निरूपण करना।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: विराम चिह्नों के गलत प्रयोग से वाक्य का अर्थ किस प्रकार अनर्थ में बदल सकता है, इसका सटीक उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: 'रोको, मत जाने दो।' (रुकने का आदेश) बनाम 'रोको मत, जाने दो।' (जाने की अनुमति) — अल्पविराम का स्थान बदलने से अर्थ पूर्णतः विपरीत हो जाता है
विराम चिह्नों से अर्थ पर कोई प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता
वाक्य केवल लंबा हो जाता है
विराम चिह्न केवल मुद्रण का सजावटी साधन हैं
explanation: अल्पविराम की स्थिति बदलने से वाक्य का अर्थ 180° उलट जाता है ('रोको, मत जाने दो' vs 'रोको मत, जाने दो')।

subject: Hindi Grammar
chapter: Chapter 12: वाक्य विचार, विराम चिह्न एवं मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियाँ
question: कक्षा 7 हिंदी व्याकरण के संपूर्ण पाठ्यक्रम का सर्वोच्च भाषाई प्रयोजन क्या है?
options: वर्ण, शब्द, संज्ञा, सर्वनाम, विशेषण, क्रिया, काल, अव्यय, संधि-समास, वाक्य-संरचना और मुहावरे-लोकोक्तियों के सम्यक ज्ञान द्वारा भाषा को व्याकरण सम्मत, प्रवाहमयी, त्रुटिहीन, प्रभावी तथा अभिव्यक्ति की दृष्टि से समृद्ध एवं सामर्थ्यवान बनाना
केवल परीक्षाओं में अंक प्राप्त करना
कठिन शब्दों को याद करके भूल जाना
प्राचीन नियमों को बिना समझे रटना
explanation: कक्षा 7 व्याकरण का समग्र उद्देश्य: विद्यार्थियों में शुद्ध वर्तनी, सुगठित वाक्य-विन्यास, अर्थगत स्पष्टता और समृद्ध अभिव्यक्ति-कौशल का पूर्ण विकास।
